summary: Montreal and Toronto chart sources join the EFB, signing in accepts a username as well as an email, and a tablet that signs in finds the PC on its own and connects with no code and no address.
releaseNotes: The EFB Charts page names the official sources for Montreal (CYUL) and Toronto (CYYZ): NAV CANADA, the CZUL index for the Montreal FIR, IVAO Canada's CAP charts and FltPlan, each opening in the publisher's own portal.
Opening Stratos on a tablet that is signed in now finds the PC on the same Wi-Fi by itself, opens the bridge the PC advertises and shows live aircraft, with no code, address or pairing step.
Signing in accepts an email address or a username, so either one created with the account works on the PC, a tablet and a phone.
The tablet reports Connected, Searching, Reconnecting or PC not found, and never shows an address or a port.
Signing in on a tablet hands the account to the local bridge with a one-time code carried in the URL fragment, which is exchanged for a bridge session and never sent to the bridge.
One PC connects automatically; several PCs on the account show a short name-only chooser, and a bridge that drops reconnects on its own.
A PC with Stratos open publishes its bridge address to the signed-in account every 30 seconds, and the record expires after two minutes so a closed PC is never offered.
Chart sources resolve per airport, so the sources offered belong to the airport's own country and region rather than to its FIR alone.
The bridge accepts a pairing link that carries a fragment, so a handed-off tablet lands on the local map instead of a cleared address.
The desktop build reads account data from the deployed account service instead of a local origin, so sign-in and discovery work in the installed app.
Automatic discovery needs the updated account service: an older one reports that bridge discovery is unavailable, and the PC's page can still be opened by hand.
Stratos links to NAV CANADA, CZUL, IVAO Canada and FltPlan and does not copy or host their documents.
Charts offered as links are the publisher's current documents, not charts bundled with Stratos.
